setlist.title: Goin' Down The Road Feeling Bad

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Valley Road** (3 reviews): Reviewer recalls dust rising and the ground shaking during it, with wicked energy; Had the whole crowd going, even with the set break interrupting it [14][16][21]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (1 review): Reviewer felt swept away by it; the band then jammed on for a very long time [20]
- **He's Gone** (1 review): The slowdown into it felt like a moving tribute to Brent, and the crowd shed tears [20]
- **Playing In The Band Reprise** (1 review): Reviewer remembers the desert, blue sky and red setting sun making a beautiful contrast during it [24]

## Setlist highlights

- **Valley Road**: rare: 7 archived performances [25]

## The recordings

- **gd1990-12-09.141607.sbd.miller.2496** (recommended): soundboard; 21 songs; 175 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd1990-12-09.sbd.gems.76477.sbeok.flac24**: soundboard; 22 songs; 177 min [2]. Said about its sound: Uploader says it is very nice and found no transfer or recording errors [2]
- **gd1990-12-09.nak300.laporte.89799.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 21 songs; 173 min [7]. Said about its sound: Different tape media makes the sound slightly different between the first and second sets [7]
- **gd90-12-09.sbd.ladner.5155.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 20 songs; 178 min; rated 4.2/5 by 15 [9]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says the recording is decent but undersells how hard the show rocked; Reviewer finds it very wet and mp3-like, resembling a diluted FM board, so not top-grade sound [14][15]
- **gd1990-12-09.157408.s1.s2p.nak-akg.cm.katz.miller.t.flac1644**: source not stated; 11 songs; 79 min [10]

## Around the show

- Warm, sunny December day; Bruce Hornsby sat in and fit the band well [14]
- Perfect weather on the grass terrace in winter; dust in the lot afterward was so thick people struggled to find cars [20]
- Beautiful desert day near the end of the tour year; Hornsby was with the band and Jerry played better [21]
- Lacks the punch of the Denver show a few nights later [16]
- Structured much like the Bonner Springs show that summer but lacks the magic of that Kansas show [22]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1990-12-09.141607.sbd.miller.2496**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK SA-X100) [1]. Also: Two sets of master tapes were combined to make the show complete [1]
- **gd1990-12-09.sbd.gems.76477.sbeok.flac24**: transferred by Todd Evans and Jamie Waddell; source: SBD > DAT(x?) [2]. Also: GEMS soundboard source with an uncut drums/space; it lacks the EAC generation [2]
- **gd1990-12-09.nak300.laporte.89799.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Chris LaPorte; transferred by Chris LaPorte; source: Nak 300's > Unknown Deck > Marantz pmd430 [7]. Also: Nak 300 cassette source; Maxell XLII 90 tape used for first set and encore, MX-s 100 for second set; Tape flips cost a few seconds of crowd noise, He's Gone and Good Lovin' [7]
- **gd90-12-09.sbd.ladner.5155.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD > DAT > CDR > WAV > SHNv3 [9]
- **gd1990-12-09.157408.s1.s2p.nak-akg.cm.katz.miller.t.flac1644**: taped by Recorded by Michael Katz patched out of my mixer; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  July 15, 2022; source: Nakamichi CM100/CP4 + AKG C1000S > Boss BX-4 Mixer > Cassette Master (Sony Boombox/TDK XLII-100) [10]. Also: Taped from the front row center taper's section; uses Michael Katz's tape 1 master since the taper's own masters were lost; Thirty-five decks were patched from the taper's feed, with Katz's boombox at the end of the line [10]
